entries.name: Christmas
entries.capsule: Birth of Jesus; part of a long Puerto Rican holiday season that runs through Three Kings Day.

dates.source: Platea PR 2026 Puerto Rico holiday calendar

entries.whatItMarks: The birth of Jesus. BORIKEN board co-chair Kenneth Ortiz told AMPERS that Puerto Rico has the longest Christmas season in the world.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: The BORIKEN Cultural Center gathers the season into one free community day, La Parranda Boricua (see separate entry). No other Minnesota Puerto Rican Christmas event was found.

entries.name: La Parranda Boricua (BORIKEN Cultural Center)
entries.capsule: BORIKEN Cultural Center's free Puerto Rican Christmas party in the Twin Cities: live music, parranda visiting songs and the Three Kings.
entries.dateRule: Set each winter by the BORIKEN Cultural Center; no fixed date was found.
entries.whatItMarks: Puerto Rico's Christmas season and the parranda custom of visiting friends with music, ending with the Three Kings.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: Free event open to all, with live music, parranda traditions, and the Reyes Magos bringing candy and gifts for children (AMPERS, Dec. 2025). BORIKEN often hosts larger gatherings in Shoreview. The Minnesota State Arts Board awarded $35,000 in FY2026 for the annual Parranda Boricua.

entries.name: Día de los Reyes
entries.capsule: The Three Kings' visit to the infant Jesus; a public holiday in Puerto Rico and a big gift day for many families.

entries.whatItMarks: The visit of the Magi; in Puerto Rico it is a public holiday and the culmination of the Christmas season.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: The Three Kings appear at BORIKEN's Parranda Boricua, bringing candy and gifts for children (AMPERS, 2025). A Roseau family told the Star Tribune in 2020 that the day, celebrated loudly at home, passed without notice in their new town.

entries.name: Hurricane María remembrance
entries.capsule: Anniversary of Hurricane María's 2017 landfall, which reshaped Puerto Rico and brought many families to Minnesota.
entries.dateRule: September 20, the anniversary of landfall in 2017. Minnesota vigils are organized by community groups when held.

dates.source: Anniversary of Sept. 20, 2017 landfall (Becoming SotaRicans StoryMap); no 2026 Minnesota vigil found

entries.whatItMarks: The September 20, 2017 landfall of Hurricane María, two weeks after Irma, and the deaths and displacement that followed.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: On Sept. 20, 2022, the fifth anniversary, about two dozen people held a vigil by the Puerto Rican mural at El Colegio High School in Minneapolis, with members of the Puerto Ricans in Minnesota Committee, and raised money after Hurricane Fiona. No 2025 or 2026 vigil was found.

entries.name: Encuentro Boricua
entries.capsule: Summer gathering of Puerto Ricans from across Minnesota, held in the Twin Cities since 2002.
entries.dateRule: Summer; set each year by local organizers. No current dates found.
entries.whatItMarks: A celebration of the Puerto Rican community in Minnesota.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: The 2022 StoryMap describes an annual summer event begun in 2002 with food, music and dance that draws hundreds of Puerto Ricans from across the state and marked its 20th anniversary in 2022. Whether it continued in 2025 or 2026 could not be confirmed.

entries.name: Hispanic Heritage Month (begins)
entries.capsule: U.S. heritage month, Sept. 15 to Oct. 15; a Latino umbrella observance, not a Puerto Rican one.
entries.whatItMarks: A national month for Hispanic and Latino Americans, September 15 to October 15.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: No Puerto Rican-specific Minnesota event was found. In 2024 Gov. Tim Walz used the month to speak of Puerto Rican and Latino families in Minnesota and Pennsylvania (Puerto Rico Report).
